title: Crude shock, bond jitters send Sensex, Nifty into a rout - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Markets suffered one of their worst sessions in months on Tuesday, as a triple blow of surging crude oil prices, multi-year highs in US bond yields and a weakening rupee sent benchmark indices sharply lower, erasing strong opening gains and closing near the day’s lows.

The BSE Sensex fell 777.94 points, or 1.04 per cent, to close at 74,003.82, having opened as high as 75,436.44 earlier in the session. The NSE Nifty 50 shed 279.50 points, or 1.19 per cent, to settle at 23,118.60, its lowest closing level since April 6, 2026, after reversing sharply from an intraday high of 23,592.85, a swing of nearly 475 points. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Smallcap 100 fell 2.1 per cent and 2.4 per cent, respectively, marking their steepest single-day decline since May 12.

Brent crude hovered near $107–108 a barrel, buoyed by fresh attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and unresolved Middle East supply concerns, while the US 10-year Treasury yield crossed 5 per cent for the first time since 2007. Back home, India’s retail inflation accelerated to a 20-month high of 4.82 per cent in August, pushing the 10-year government bond yield up 7 basis points to 7.09 per cent, a four-month high.

“Domestic markets remained under pressure, extending their recent correction as elevated crude oil prices and rising global bond yields weighed on sentiment,” said Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments. “...concerns about a prolonged high-interest-rate environment, particularly in the US, kept Treasury yields near multi-year highs and continued to dampen emerging market sentiment amid persistent foreign outflows.”

The sell-off was sweeping. Of the 500 stocks in the Nifty 500 universe, 434 ended in the red. Market breadth on the BSE deteriorated sharply, with the advance-decline ratio falling to 0.36. India VIX, the market’s fear gauge, surged more than 9 per cent to close at 13.4.

IT was the sole bright spot. The Nifty IT index gained 2.2 per cent, as comments from the leadership of OpenAI and Anthropic calling for a more measured pace of AI development eased concerns about rapid disruption to Indian IT services. HCL Technologies, Infosys and TCS were among the top Nifty 50 gainers. On the other end, Nifty Realty tumbled over 4 per cent, Nifty Metal fell 2.5 per cent, and Nifty Defence declined 6 per cent amid profit-booking after an 18 per cent run this year. BEL and Shriram Finance were the session’s biggest laggards.

Tata Group stocks remained in focus after the RBI rejected Tata Sons’ request to surrender its registration as a core investment company, reviving expectations of a potential public listing and triggering a rally across listed Tata entities.

Solar Industries dropped 13 per cent after announcing a ₹12,951 crore all-cash acquisition of South Africa’s Omnia Holdings, a deal the market found difficult to absorb given the prevailing environment.

The rupee extended its losing streak into a fifth consecutive session, closing at 95.96 against the dollar, a depreciation of 40 paise, as global bond yield pressures and rising crude weighed on the currency. The spot USD/INR pair faces resistance at 96.30, with support at 95.45, with the bias favouring dollar bulls, according to Dilip Parmar, Research Analyst at HDFC Securities.

All eyes now turn to the US Federal Reserve’s September 15–16 policy meeting, with the rate decision due Wednesday. NSE’s IPO, one of India’s largest-ever public issues at ₹22,562 crore, opens Thursday, its reception in this environment will be a test of underlying investor conviction. Until the Fed delivers its verdict, analysts say, any recovery attempt in the market is likely to be met with fresh selling.
